correctness.rationale: At a fixed world, zero-weight worlds contribute 1 to Box and 0 to Diamond. Thus a finite positive row support suffices for Box, including the all-zero row since the world set is nonempty. For infinite support choose distinct positive-weight worlds and assign the atom min(R/2,1/(n+1)) there and 1 elsewhere; the residuals are all positive and have unattained infimum zero. For Diamond, when the supremum d is positive, only the finite superlevel at d/2 can contribute values above d/2; when d is zero any world witnesses it. An infinite superlevel at delta instead admits atomic values delta*n/(n+1) on distinct worlds from that level and 0 elsewhere, giving unattained supremum delta. Because formula-value functions are a subset of arbitrary scalar functions and atoms realize every scalar input, these are exact criteria at all modal depths. The decaying 1/n row separates them. The frozen verification and script were inspected, not executed; the finite extrema enumeration and finite prefixes do not prove the infinite statements.
residual_risks: The countably infinite selections use ordinary choice. A semantics requiring a positive-weight witness changes the all-zero row case; it is explicitly excluded here.
